candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Management of Care, printed p.7 / PDF p.11
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize unresolved understanding as a reason to pause a procedure and obtain additional informed-consent discussion.

options.A: Pause the process and notify the responsible practitioner so the client can receive the information needed for an informed decision
options.B: Tell the client the signature alone proves informed consent and proceed
options.C: Provide reassurance that no additional explanation is necessary once the form is signed
options.D: Ask a family member to decide what the client should understand without involving the practitioner

candidate.rationale: CMS hospital informed-consent guidance requires hospital policies, processes, and forms to provide information that permits the patient or representative to make fully informed decisions about care. A signed form does not cure an unresolved lack of understanding. The nurse should pause and obtain clarification from the responsible practitioner rather than treating the signature as sufficient.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Supports the requirement that consent processes provide enough information for patients/representatives to make fully informed decisions.
candidate.source_document_title: QSO-24-10-Hospitals: Revisions and Clarifications to Hospital Interpretive Guidelines for Informed Consent
candidate.stem: Immediately before a procedure requiring informed consent, a client tells the nurse, "I signed the form, but I still don't understand what they're going to do or what the alternatives are." What should the nurse do?
